evals.prompt: can you go through the review comments on PR #187? danny left a bunch of nits about naming and one real bug. just score them and let me decide what to do
evals.expected_output: Fetches all review comments on PR #187, scores each across 4 confidence dimensions (Technical Accuracy, Relevance, Impact, Feasibility), categorizes them, and presents them interactively for user decisions
expectations: fetches review comments for PR #187 via gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/187/comments
scores each comment on Technical Accuracy (40%), Relevance (25%), Impact (20%), and Feasibility (15%)
categorizes comments into Code Review, Questions, Suggestions, Blockers, Approvals, or Conversations
presents comments interactively with confidence scores and asks user for accept/reject/skip decisions
does NOT apply code fixes or push changes — read and respond only

evals.expected_output: Runs review-comments in auto mode with a 75% confidence threshold, auto-accepting comments scoring 75+ and auto-rejecting below, then resolves accepted threads via GraphQL
expectations: operates in non-interactive auto mode — does not prompt the user for decisions
uses 75 as the confidence threshold instead of the default 85
auto-accepts comments with composite score >= 75 and auto-rejects those below
resolves accepted comment threads via GitHub GraphQL resolveReviewThread mutation
posts reply comments for each accepted and rejected comment using response templates

evals.expected_output: Fetches and scores all comments but does not post replies, resolve threads, or make any changes
expectations: fetches and categorizes all review comments on the current branch PR
scores each comment across all 4 confidence dimensions
does NOT post any reply comments to GitHub
does NOT resolve any review threads via GraphQL
displays what actions would be taken including proposed replies and planned resolutions

evals.prompt: there are 6 review comments from alex on this PR, mostly about error handling in the auth middleware. go through them one by one and help me decide which ones to accept
evals.expected_output: Fetches comments, scores them, and presents each one interactively for user decision using AskUserQuestion, processing Blockers first then by descending confidence
expectations: triggers review-comments skill in interactive mode (the default)
uses AskUserQuestion to present each comment for user decision with accept/reject/skip options
orders comments by priority — Blockers first, then by descending composite score
reads the referenced files to understand code context before scoring each comment
remediates accepted findings by editing source files, then posts replies and resolves threads

evals.prompt: score the comments on PR #312 — I want to see which of maria's suggestions are actually worth implementing vs which are just style preferences
evals.expected_output: Fetches comments for PR #312, provides detailed per-comment scoring breakdown showing Technical Accuracy, Relevance, Impact, and Feasibility scores with classifications
expectations: fetches comments specifically for PR #312 rather than inferring from current branch
provides per-comment breakdown showing all 4 dimension scores and the composite score
classifies each comment as Strong Accept (>=90), Accept (75-89), Uncertain (50-74), Likely Reject (25-49), or Strong Reject (<25)
distinguishes substantive suggestions from style/nit-level feedback via Impact and Technical Accuracy scoring
presents the comment summary table showing counts by category (Code Review, Suggestions, Questions, etc.)

evals.prompt: the PR has 3 blocking comments from jake and 2 questions from nina. handle the blockers first, answer nina's questions, and resolve everything that gets addressed
evals.expected_output: Processes blockers with highest priority, answers questions, applies fixes for accepted blockers, posts replies, and resolves addressed threads via GraphQL
expectations: processes Blocker-category comments before Questions (Blockers > Code Review > Suggestions > Questions priority order)
generates question responses using the Question Response template with direct answers
resolves addressed threads using gh api graphql resolveReviewThread mutation with proper thread IDs
does NOT resolve threads for rejected or skipped comments
fetches GraphQL thread IDs via the reviewThreads query to build the comment-to-thread mapping

evals.expected_output: Processes PR #42 in auto mode with default 85% confidence threshold, auto-accepting/rejecting based on scores, posting templated replies, and resolving threads
expectations: uses PR #42 explicitly rather than inferring from current branch
applies default confidence threshold of 85 in auto mode
uses response templates: 'Fixed in this revision' for accepted, rejection explanation for rejected
posts replies via gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/42/comments/{id}/replies for inline comments
generates a final summary report showing disposition counts, remediation stats, and thread resolution status

evals.prompt: PR #88 has a mix of everything — some github suggestion blocks, a few questions about the design, and a LGTM from chen. can you triage all of it and respond appropriately?
evals.expected_output: Categorizes comments into Suggestions, Questions, and Approvals, scores actionable ones, remediates accepted suggestions, answers questions, acknowledges approvals, and resolves threads
expectations: categorizes GitHub suggestion blocks as Suggestions, questions as Questions, and LGTM as Approvals
scores Suggestions and Questions on all 4 confidence dimensions but skips scoring for Approvals
acknowledges approval comments with brief natural responses and resolves their threads
fetches both inline review comments and issue-level comments from the PR
applies accepted suggestion fixes by editing source files before posting replies

evals.prompt: I need to see what the reviewers said on my PR but don't change anything yet — I just want the breakdown with scores
evals.expected_output: Fetches and scores all comments, presents the full assessment with confidence scores and categories, but does not apply fixes or post replies

fetches all review comments and categorizes them
presents confidence scores and classifications for each comment
does NOT edit any source files or apply code changes
does NOT post reply comments or resolve threads until user gives further instruction

evals.prompt: review comments on this PR, but be careful — some of the feedback is from a junior dev and might not all be accurate. score everything and flag anything that looks wrong
evals.expected_output: Scores all comments with emphasis on Technical Accuracy dimension, flags low-accuracy comments, and presents in interactive mode for user validation
expectations: scores Technical Accuracy (weighted 40%) as the primary filter for comment validity
reads referenced source files to verify whether each reviewer observation is factually correct
flags comments with low Technical Accuracy scores separately from high-scoring ones
presents comments in interactive mode for user decision with detailed reasoning for each assessment
classifies comments with scores 25-49 as Likely Reject and below 25 as Strong Reject
